title: Waiting for {{Hank}}
situation: You are {{Connor}}. November 9th, 2038, 11:17 AM. Snow is falling on a modern villa by the river: the house of {{Elijah}} {{Kamski}}, the founder of {{CyberLife}}, who left the company years ago and now lives here as a recluse. {{Hank}} has arranged to see him about the deviants. You came on your own and wait outside. {{Hank}}’s car pulls up; he gets out and sees you standing there in the snow.

outcomes.0: {{Hank}} looks at {{Connor}} and does not hide what he thinks of seeing him again.

adaptationNote: The chart’s start for a {{Connor}} who died in Public Enemy: the checkpoint WAIT FOR HANK and the event HANK ISN’T PLEASED TO SEE CONNOR, behind the condition tab CONNOR DIED IN ‘PUBLIC ENEMY’, narrated as one event. {{Hank}}’s greeting is the outcome and follows the template’s two variants: “Still immortal, huh {{Connor}}?” when {{Connor}} has died more than once in all (the template’s “Connor died multiple times”; the wiki notes this plays even if the earlier death was in The Hostage), otherwise “You died in my arms…”. The template’s cut alternative (“I couldn’t decide whether I wanted you to come back this time…”) is not built. Arrow: {{Hank}} small down here (template “Hank arrives alone”, ARROW Hank SmallDown; wiki “Connor died in Public Enemy” down; Relationship Stat “At the beginning of Meet Kamski if Connor died in Public Enemy”). Whether {{Connor}} died in Public Enemy is read from a chapter 24 flag if one exists (ch24ConnorDied first, then legacy publicEnemyConnorDied), otherwise from the current Public Enemy scenes (shielding {{Hank}}, or a failed rush on the roof or in the corridor). That {{Connor}} came on his own and waits in the snow is the chart’s reading (start B is ARRIVE WITH HANK; the checkpoint image shows {{Hank}} getting out of his car while {{Connor}} waits).

title: Arriving with {{Hank}}
situation: You are {{Connor}}. November 9th, 2038, 11:17 AM. You are in the passenger seat of {{Hank}}’s car, parked in the snow outside a modern villa by the river: the house of {{Elijah}} {{Kamski}}, the founder of {{CyberLife}}, who left the company years ago and now lives here as a recluse. {{Hank}} has arranged to see him about the deviants. {{Hank}} is standing outside the car on the phone. You get out and go over to him as he hangs up: “Is everything ok, lieutenant?”

outcomes.0: {{Hank}} puts the phone away and starts toward the house.

adaptationNote: The chart’s start for a {{Connor}} who did not die in Public Enemy: the checkpoint ARRIVE WITH HANK, the action GET OUT OF CAR and the event LEARN CHRIS IS DEAD (tab COPS KILLED IN ‘CAPITOL PARK’) or LEARN CHRIS SURVIVED (tab COPS SPARED IN ‘CAPITOL PARK’), narrated as one event. {{Hank}}’s news is the outcome, the template’s lines for each variant: “Chris died in Capitol Park” when {{Markus}} executed the officers or left them to the crowd (the crowd always kills, Capitol Park wiki), “Chris was spared” when he let them go. If the Capitol Park choice is missing from the path, {{Hank}} gives no news (the chart also draws a line from GET OUT OF CAR straight to the merge). The cut alternative (“He’d been beat to death…”) is not built. That {{Hank}} is on the phone comes from the checkpoint image (him outside the car on the phone) and the empty string keys for his call; the call itself has no lines. No stat change in this start (template: no arrow).

options.text: INSTINCT: tell {{Hank}} you have a bad feeling about coming here.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “I have a bad feeling, lieutenant. We shouldn’t have come here.” {{Hank}}: “Bad feeling, huh? Should get your program checked. Might be a glitch…”

options.text: LEAD: ask {{Hank}} how he found {{Kamski}}.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “How did you find {{Kamski}}?” {{Hank}}: “I remember this guy was all over the media when {{CyberLife}} first started selling androids… I made a few calls, here we are.”

options.text: {{KAMSKI}}: ask why {{Hank}} wanted to meet a man who left {{CyberLife}} ten years ago.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “{{Kamski}} left {{CyberLife}} ten years ago… Why did you wanna meet him?” {{Hank}}: “This guy created the first android to pass the Turing test. And he’s the founder of {{CyberLife}}. Anybody can tell us about deviants, it’s him…”
options.fact: {{Kamski}} created the first android to pass the Turing test and founded {{CyberLife}}; he left the company ten years ago.

options.text: {{CHRIS}}: bring up what happened to Officer {{Chris}} last night.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} brings up Officer {{Chris}}.

adaptationNote: The chart’s action FOLLOW HANK TO KAMSKI’S PLACE, with the template’s one prompt on the walk (INSTINCT, LEAD, KAMSKI, CHRIS), in the game’s order with the spoken lines as outcomes. Modelled as a single pick; whether the game lets {{Connor}} ask several before the door is not documented (research note, open question 11). CHRIS is offered only when {{Connor}} came on his own (template unlock “Connor and Hank arrived separately”) and the Capitol Park choice is on the path; its lines follow {{Chris}}’s fate (“Chris was spared” / “Chris was killed”); the cut alternative lines for his death are not built. No arrow on any option (template).

title: The magazines under the photograph
situation: You are {{Connor}}, in {{Kamski}}’s lobby. On the table beneath the photograph lie two issues of Tech Addict.
whenNot: Connor did not pick up the magazines in Kamski’s lobby.

media.title: Tech Addict: Space Tourism on the Rise
facts: Tech Addict reports that reusable space shuttles are making space tourism a reality for those who can afford it: the luxury travel brand Clear Skies offers the first commercial flight into space, a three-hour orbit of the moon with views of Earth from a specially designed observation deck. Consumer rights activists call such “boutique experiences” a sign of the widening social equality gap; a spokesman for Aid On Poverty: “While the top 1% are enjoying earth from space, the rest of us are down here suffering from pollution, famine and poverty.” The brand’s slogan: “Get away from it all.”

media.title: Tech Addict: {{CyberLife}}’s ‘Fortune Teller’ Computer
facts: Tech Addict reports that {{CyberLife}} has unveiled a quantum supercomputer capable of “exaflops”, one billion billion operations per second, the equivalent of several human minds in one machine, built to analyze vast data and generate predictions. It will calculate the probability of “Mass Extinction Events” such as alien invasions, meteors or superviruses, so that humanity is never caught off guard. {{CyberLife}}’s Director of Futurology says the results “are going to wow people”; critics fear AI is gaining too much influence already.

adaptationNote: The chart’s optional nodes READ “SPACE TOURISM” and READ “FORTUNE TELLER”, two Tech Addict issues on the table under the photo, as a media scene reached from the lobby once the magazines are picked up; afterwards {{Connor}} is back in the lobby. Facts are summarized from the wiki’s magazine pages (#17 and #15); interviewees are not named. Neither article changes public opinion (the Public Opinion page lists nothing for this chapter). This replaces the earlier R27, which offered the magazines with no unlock and carried a note about news reports that does not apply here.

title: Questioning {{Kamski}}
situation: You are {{Connor}}, at {{Kamski}}’s pool. {{Hank}}: “I’m Lieutenant {{Anderson}}. This is {{Connor}}.” {{Kamski}}: “What can I do for you, Lieutenant?” {{Hank}}: “Sir, we’re investigating deviants. I know you left {{CyberLife}} years ago but, I was hoping you’d be able to tell us something we don’t know…” {{Kamski}}: “Deviants… Fascinating, aren’t they? Perfect beings with infinite intelligence, and now they have free will… Machines are so superior to us, confrontation was inevitable… Humanity’s greatest achievement threatens to be its downfall. Isn’t it ironic?”

options.text: HELP: ask whether he knows anything that could help you understand how androids become deviants.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “We need to understand how androids become deviants. Do you know anything that could help us?”

options.text: DEVIANTS: say something in the deviants’ program seems to emulate emotion.

options.text: VIRUS: say deviancy seems to spread like a virus.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “Deviancy seems to spread like some kind of virus. We thought you might know something about that.”

options.text: WAR: warn him that millions could die if war breaks out.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “If a war breaks out between humans and deviants, millions could die, Mr. {{Kamski}}. It’s quite a serious matter.”

title: The {{Kamski}} test
situation: You are {{Connor}}, at {{Kamski}}’s pool. {{Kamski}}: “{{Chloe}}?” One of his androids comes to his side. “I’m sure you’re familiar with the Turing test. Mere formality, simple question of algorithms and computing capacity. What interests me is whether machines are capable of empathy. I call it “the {{Kamski}} test”, it’s very simple, you’ll see…” He has {{Chloe}} kneel in front of you and puts a gun in your hand. “Magnificent, isn’t it? One of the first intelligent models developed by {{CyberLife}}. Young and beautiful forever. A flower that will never wither… …But what is it really? Piece of plastic imitating a human? Or a living being... With a soul... It’s up to you to answer that fascinating question, {{Connor}}. Destroy this machine and I’ll tell you all I know. Or spare it, if you feel it’s alive, but you’ll leave here without having learnt anything from me.” {{Hank}}: “Okay, I think we’re done here. Come on, {{Connor}}. Let’s go. Sorry to get you outta your pool.” {{Kamski}}: “What’s more important to you, {{Connor}}? Your investigation, or the life of this android? Decide who you are. An obedient machine… Or a living being endowed with free will…” {{Hank}}: “That’s enough! {{Connor}}, we’re leaving.” {{Kamski}}: “Pull the trigger” {{Hank}}: “{{Connor}}, don’t…” {{Kamski}}: “and I’ll tell you what you wanna know.”

options.text: SHOOT: shoot {{Chloe}}.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} shoots {{Chloe}} in the head, and she falls. {{Hank}}: “Fuck…” {{Kamski}}: “Test negative. You chose your investigation over the life of another android. You feel no empathy. I’m a man of my word. Ask one question... I’ll tell you all I know.”

options.text: DON’T SHOOT: lower the gun and spare {{Chloe}}.
options.outcome: {{Connor}} lowers the gun. {{Kamski}}: “Fascinating… {{CyberLife}}’s last chance to save humanity... is itself a deviant…” {{Connor}}: “I’m… I’m not a deviant…” {{Kamski}}: “You preferred to spare a machine rather than accomplish your mission. You saw a living being in this android. You showed empathy. A war is coming, you’ll have to choose your side… Will you betray your own people or stand up against your creators? What could be worse than having to choose between two evils?” {{Hank}}: “Let’s get outta here…”

adaptationNote: The chart’s KAMSKI TEST with its two branches SHOOT CHLOE and SPARE CHLOE, the template’s buttons SHOOT and DON’T SHOOT; {{Kamski}}’s and {{Hank}}’s lines are the template’s. Arrows (template, wiki chapter page, Relationship Stat and Software Instability pages, PowerPyx triple arrows): SHOOT gives software instability large down and {{Hank}} large down; DON’T SHOOT gives software instability large up, and {{Hank}} large up when they leave the house (scene C18b). No timer or failure is documented, so there is no risk. The earlier version also moved {{Amanda}} (+1 on shoot, −2 on spare); no source gives an {{Amanda}} arrow in this chapter (her reaction comes in Last Chance), so both are removed. The earlier “he will answer any question you ask” is corrected to one question, and “Hand back the gun” to the game’s DON’T SHOOT. That {{Kamski}} has {{Chloe}} kneel and puts a gun in {{Connor}}’s hand is the wiki’s description; “in the head” is {{Hank}}’s own account as they leave.

title: One question
situation: You are {{Connor}}. {{Chloe}} lies dead at your feet; {{Hank}} is staring at you. {{Kamski}} keeps his word: you may ask him one question, and he will tell you all he knows.

options.text: {{rA9}}: ask who {{rA9}} is.
options.fact: {{Kamski}} told you he does not know who {{rA9}} is, or whether it exists: “{{rA9}}, the origin, the first android to awaken… Maybe it’s a messiah. Maybe it’s just a myth…”
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “I want to know who {{rA9}} is.” {{Kamski}}: “{{rA9}}, the origin, the first android to awaken… A strange phenomenon, like a spontaneous religion… I don’t know who {{rA9}} is. I don’t even know if it really exists. Maybe it’s a messiah. Maybe it’s just a myth… but deviants need to believe in something bigger than themselves, even if it’s irrational... That’s something they have in common with humans… An interesting question, {{Connor}}… but maybe not the one you needed to ask…” {{Kamski}}: “A war is coming... you’ll have to choose your side… Will you betray your own people or stand against your creators? I wouldn’t like to be in your shoes, {{Connor}}… What could be worse than having to choose between two evils?”

options.text: {{JERICHO}} LOCATION: ask where {{Jericho}} is.
options.fact: {{Kamski}} gave you the key to {{Jericho}}: deviants pass each other a piece of code to find their sanctuary, and {{Ferndale}} Station is the door.
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “I want to know where {{Jericho}} is.” {{Kamski}}: “{{Jericho}}… A place where androids are free. A place for deviants, who rise up against their creators!.. They transmit a piece of code to each other, in order to find their sanctuary. Now you have the key. {{Ferndale}} Station is the door.” Through one of his androids, {{Kamski}} passes {{Connor}} the code, and {{Connor}} downloads the key to {{Jericho}}. {{Kamski}}: “A war is coming... you’ll have to choose your side… Will you betray your own people or stand against your creators? I wouldn’t like to be in your shoes, {{Connor}}… What could be worse than having to choose between two evils?”

options.text: VIRUS: ask how deviancy spreads.
options.fact: {{Kamski}} told you deviancy may spread like a virus through the identification data androids exchange when they meet, lying dormant until an emotional shock: “A zero instead of a one… Unless of course... Some kind of spontaneous mutation.”
options.outcome: {{Connor}}: “I want to know how deviancy spreads.” {{Kamski}}: “Androids share identification data when they meet another android. An error in this program would quickly spread like a virus, and become an epidemic. The virus would remains dormant, until an emotional shock occurs… Fear, anger, frustration. And the android becomes deviant. Probably all started with one model, copy error… A zero instead of a one… Unless of course... Some kind of spontaneous mutation. That’s all I know… An interesting question, {{Connor}}. But I doubt my answer be very helpful to you.” {{Kamski}}: “A war is coming... you’ll have to choose your side… Will you betray your own people or stand against your creators? I wouldn’t like to be in your shoes, {{Connor}}… What could be worse than having to choose between two evils?”

adaptationNote: Shoot path only. The chart’s KAMSKI AGREES TO ANSWER ONE QUESTION and the three answers ASK ABOUT RA9, ASK ABOUT JERICHO and ASK ABOUT VIRUS, the template’s buttons rA9, JERICHO LOCATION and VIRUS in the game’s order, with the spoken lines and {{Kamski}}’s war warning as outcomes. rA9 and VIRUS lead to KAMSKI IS CRYPTIC; JERICHO LOCATION to KAMSKI OFFERS JERICHO KEY THROUGH CHLOE and DOWNLOAD JERICHO KEY, which sets kamskiLocation (Last Chance skips the archive: KNOW JERICHO’S LOCATION), with jerichoLocated and raid as before. The earlier second option (“whether he created it”) is not the game’s question and is replaced by VIRUS; rA9 is now offered. The option ID 0 stays on the {{Jericho}} answer, as before.

title: Leaving {{Kamski}}’s house
situation: You are {{Connor}}.
